name: Gaistal Leutasch
kurzbeschreibung: The Gaistal valley near Leutasch at over 1,200 m: untouched alpine pasture paradise between Wetterstein and Mieminger Chain, Ganghoferweg trail and Igelsee lake.
beschreibung:
Overview

The wild and romantic Gaistal valley is a breathtaking high valley in the North Tyrolean Limestone Alps, located in the municipality of Leutasch at an altitude between 1,200 and 1,600 meters above sea level. Framed by the towering south faces of the mighty Wetterstein Mountains with the Zugspitze to the north and the rugged peaks of the Mieminger Chain with the Hohe Munde to the south, the valley is considered one of the most unspoiled high valleys in the entire Eastern Alps. The crystal-clear Leutascher Ache river winds through the car-free valley, past lush alpine meadows, rustic huts, and dense larch forests.

Route & Requirements

The Gaistal valley has a long tradition as a grazing area and is reverently referred to by hikers and cyclists as the “Valley of the Alpine Pastures”: over ten managed alpine pastures and mountain huts – including the Hämmermoosalm, the Gaistalalm, the Tillfussalm, and the Knorrhütte – invite visitors to stop for a cozy break. The valley gained cultural fame through the Bavarian regional writer Ludwig Ganghofer (1855–1920): Ganghofer spent many summers in his secluded hunting lodge Hubertus near the Tillfussalm, where he wrote world-famous novels such as “Das Schweigen im Walde” (The Silence in the Forest). Today, the approximately 14-kilometer-long Ganghoferweg trail commemorates the writer's work.

Visit & Arrival

The Gaistal valley is freely and cost-free accessible all year round; most alpine huts are open from mid-May to the end of October. In winter, selected huts offer winter hiking and tobogganing. The valley itself is completely closed to general motor vehicle traffic. Arrival by car is from Innsbruck or Munich via Seefeld in Tirol through the Leutaschtal valley to the hamlet of Klamm and further to the large hiking car park Salzbach / Gaistal at the valley entrance. This is subject to a fee (day ticket approx. €6.00). By public transport, you can reach the Gaistal valley via the ÖBB train station Seefeld in Tirol. From there, the regional VVT bus line 430 runs hourly directly to the final stop Leutasch Salzbach / Gaistal.

Tips

The main path through the Gaistal valley is wide and gravelled, rises only gently, and is ideal for family outings with all-terrain strollers as well as for leisure cyclists with e-bikes. Numerous battery charging stations are available at the alpine pastures. Stop at the Tillfussalm and try homemade Tyrolean bacon dumplings or fresh buttermilk directly from the grazing alpine cows. The Gaistal valley offers a perfect combination of nature experience and culinary delight in one of Tyrol's most beautiful landscapes.
preis: Free access (parking at the valley entrance subject to charge)
oeffnungszeiten: Open year-round; alpine huts open mid-May to end of October
